name: Fiscal conservatism
summary: Fiscal conservatism is the economic strand of conservatism, built on capitalism, limited government and laissez-faire. It favors lower taxes, restrained spending, balanced budgets, deregulation, privatization and free trade, and treats public debt as a burden on future citizens. Factions differ on priorities: deficit hawks, supply-siders and spending reducers.
scope: The mainstream American tradition as set out by Barry Goldwater (The Conscience of a Conservative, 1960), Milton Friedman (Capitalism and Freedom, 1962) and Ronald Reagan's 1981 inaugural address, together with the general account in the Wikipedia article. It is an economic philosophy, so most social, cultural and foreign-policy statements are not settled by it and are answered neutral or low-confidence.

keyFigures.name: Barry Goldwater

keyFigures.name: Milton Friedman
keyFigures.role: Economist who argued for free markets, a monetary rule and school vouchers in Capitalism and Freedom.

keyFigures.name: Ronald Reagan
keyFigures.role: President who cut top tax rates and called government the problem.

sources.usedFor: Friedman's positions on markets, money, trade, vouchers, welfare and licensing.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Fiscal conservatives oppose large new tax-funded entitlements; Goldwater wanted welfare-type provision left to families, churches and charities, and Friedman called state programs inefficient.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Not a core fiscal issue; inferred from the free-market preference for letting wages be set by employers and workers, a view in line with Friedman's market-first stance.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Free markets and laissez-faire are named as the philosophical base, and Friedman argues markets coordinate better than government control.

public-ownership.rationale: Privatization is a listed goal, and Friedman limits government to law, property and money.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Lower taxes are the movement's signature aim; Goldwater rejects graduated rates as unjust and Reagan said taxes penalize achievement.

unions-good.rationale: Little said directly; inferred from the preference for market wage-setting and the movement's link to right-to-work and restrictions on union power, though some adherents stay neutral.

property-fundamental.rationale: Goldwater treats property and earnings as inseparable from freedom, and taxation is framed as a property-rights question.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Deregulation is a defining goal, and Friedman opposes even occupational licensing as protection for insiders.

cut-welfare.rationale: Goldwater wanted the welfare state dismantled and Friedman called many programs misguided, though some adherents accept a safety net such as Friedman's negative income tax.

worker-ownership.rationale: Not a state matter, but mandated collective ownership departs from capitalism as the base; voluntary employee ownership is not opposed, so only a mild disagree.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Fiscal conservatism has no position; adherents split between security hawks and civil-libertarian limited-government types.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Friedman opposed the war on drugs, but mainstream fiscal conservatives in the Republican mould are divided, so the movement is genuinely split.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Inferred from limited-government principles that favor narrow state powers over speech; not addressed by the economic philosophy.

strong-leader.rationale: Inferred from Reagan's stress on government drawing power from the people and from constitutional limits; the economic philosophy is silent.

state-harmful.rationale: They want a smaller state, not none: Reagan said he did not mean to abolish government, and Friedman gives it core functions.

limit-guns.rationale: Outside fiscal doctrine; inferred from the movement's usual alignment with limited government in the US, though not a core tenet.

empower-police-military.rationale: Split: Goldwater wanted military superiority, but deficit hawks and spending reducers target defense budgets too, and Reagan's defense rise fed deficits.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not an economic question; libertarian-leaning adherents say yes and social conservatives no.

decide-locally.rationale: Reagan and Goldwater stress that states precede the federal government and oppose federal grants and intervention in areas reserved to states.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed; adherents divide between cost-minded reform and tough punishment.

traditional-family.rationale: Fiscal conservatism is the economic strand, and the movement mixes social conservatives with socially liberal libertarians.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: An economic philosophy with no stance; adherents split by social views.

abortion-legal.rationale: No position in the economic philosophy; adherents divide.

more-religion-public.rationale: Not a fiscal matter; adherents range from religious conservatives to secular libertarians.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Inferred: affirmative redistribution programs conflict with the preference for limited spending and equal treatment, though not a defining issue.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Outside the economic philosophy; no shared position.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Not part of fiscal doctrine, and free-trade and libertarian adherents are cool on cultural nationalism.

gradual-change.rationale: Reagan sought to reverse government growth, which is not cautious gradualism, while Goldwater proposed staged cuts; no settled view.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Split: market liberals favor labor mobility while others stress welfare costs; the economic philosophy does not settle it.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Goldwater opposed deferring to the UN and complained of its cost to the US; limited government extends to supranational bodies.

free-trade.rationale: Free trade is listed among the core goals, and Friedman wants trade barriers and quotas removed.

nation-first.rationale: Goldwater put national interest first in aid and UN matters, but free-trade adherents favor global exchange; split.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Goldwater would limit foreign commitments and aid to national interest; spending reducers dislike costly missions, though hawks differ.

open-borders.rationale: Friedman-style market liberals like open labor markets but deny open borders alongside welfare; mainstream adherents mildly disagree.

limit-growth.rationale: The movement centres on growth through tax cuts and low regulation, so limiting growth runs against its core economic aim.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Inferred: costly government programs and regulation conflict with the deregulation and spending-reduction agenda.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Markets are trusted to innovate, but no stated view on technology as solution.

expand-nuclear.rationale: No stated position; market advocates prefer private choice and dislike subsidies.

revolution-justified.rationale: Inferred from Reagan's constitutional, consent-based framing and the movement's reformist politics.

experts-over-public.rationale: Friedman distrusts technocratic discretion, favoring fixed rules over expert judgment, so adherents lean against expert rule.

central-planning.rationale: Government control of production is rejected, and Friedman argues it undermines freedom.

socialized-markets.rationale: Market exchange is accepted, but the ownership condition is not required; adherents prefer private business and oppose public ownership.

land-value-tax.rationale: A single tax replacing others is not a standard position; Friedman liked a flat income tax with few deductions instead.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Lower taxes and property rights are central; Goldwater treats taxation of wealth as a property-rights concern.

basic-income.rationale: Friedman proposed a negative income tax to replace programs but with conditions tied to income; a universal unconditional income is costly and opposed by most.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Free trade is a core goal; the article notes tariffs belonged to 19th-century classical liberals, not the modern movement.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Directing investment is planning and is rejected; Reagan said the state should foster productivity, not direct it.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Private property is prized but concentration is not an issue; adherents are indifferent.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Contradicts the capitalist base of the philosophy.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Friedman criticized the Fed's record but proposed a rule for it rather than abolition, and most adherents keep central banks.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-set wages and prices contradict laissez-faire and market pricing.

one-party-rule.rationale: Reagan's consent-of-the-governed framing and Friedman's link between freedom and markets reject one-party rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Burke is cited as an early voice, but modern fiscal conservatism takes no stance on monarchy.

democracy-best.rationale: Reagan grounds government in the people's consent; an inference since the economic philosophy is not about regime form.

direct-votes.rationale: Inferred: adherents favor constitutional limits, though ballot measures on taxes have been popular; mildly against.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils replacing parliaments are far from the movement and run against private enterprise.

right-to-secede.rationale: Not addressed; Reagan said the states created the federal government, but that is not a secession claim.

political-violence-never.rationale: Not addressed by the economic philosophy; adherents divide on how absolute to be.

natural-rulers.rationale: Inferred from the consent-based view of government; no stated position.

war-builds-character.rationale: Inferred: war is costly and spending-reducers oppose it; no stated position.

separate-church-state.rationale: Not addressed; adherents range from religious conservatives to secularists.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Not an economic position; limited-government adherents lean against scripture-based law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Friedman and Goldwater assign law, justice and defense to government as its core functions, so privatizing them is a libertarian step beyond the mainstream.

military-superiority.rationale: Goldwater insists mere parity will not do against the Soviets, and Reagan raised defense spending, though deficit hawks object to its cost.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Inferred: market liberalism is indifferent to ethnicity, and Friedman notes markets ignore personal traits; not a stated position.

class-struggle-history.rationale: A capitalist, harmony-of-exchange philosophy rejects class conflict as the driver of history; Friedman stresses mutual benefit in voluntary exchange.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Goldwater and Friedman oppose redistribution and graduated taxes aimed at equalizing results.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: No stated view; property-rights principles cut both ways.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred from opposition to transfers and foreign aid beyond the national interest.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred from preference for limited government and national self-governance; not discussed.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Voluntary exchange for mutual benefit and the free-market base imply self-interest is legitimate, though adherents do not all call it a moral good.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Property and individual freedom are central in Goldwater, so rights-first is favored, but Burkean adherents differ.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: No position from the economic philosophy.

limit-population.rationale: Compulsory limits conflict with limited government; economic philosophy otherwise silent.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The movement is pro-growth and pro-capitalism, which rejects the claim.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Markets are trusted but no stated position on speeding disruption; adherents split.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not addressed; libertarian-leaning adherents say yes, social conservatives no.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Friedman prefers fixed rules to discretion, but rule by AI expands government decision-making, which they distrust.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not addressed by fiscal doctrine; adherents split between security and liberty.

restore-past-order.rationale: The movement seeks to reverse government growth, but it is not a general restorationism, so only a mild disagree.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Adherents are principled about limited government, while Friedman judged policies by empirical results; split.

direct-action.rationale: Inferred from a constitutional, electoral approach such as Reagan's and the Contract with America.

means-match-ends.rationale: The sources discuss fiscal means, not the match between means and ends, so adherents have no shared view.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Pro-capitalist, pro-growth philosophy rejects a return to foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Market exchange rests on specialization, which Friedman defends.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Goldwater and Friedman reject distribution by need in favor of earnings and markets.

production-for-use.rationale: Profit-driven markets are the base of the philosophy.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Profit is seen as the legitimate return of voluntary exchange, not exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Opposed to socialism and to dictatorship; Reagan grounds power in consent.

collective-farming.rationale: Goldwater wants farm subsidies ended and the market to decide farming; collectivization is the opposite.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The movement holds that markets and free trade promote prosperity and peace; Friedman ties economic to political freedom.

taxation-theft.rationale: They want lower taxes but accept taxation: Goldwater says government may claim an equal percentage of wealth, so the stronger libertarian claim is rejected.

harm-principle.rationale: No stated view; libertarians say yes and social conservatives no.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Goldwater and Friedman centre the individual, though the philosophy does not address group rights directly.

conscription.rationale: Friedman proposed a volunteer military in Capitalism and Freedom, so adherents lean against conscription.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not addressed; Friedman values choice and competition but no stated ranking.

state-as-business.rationale: Adherents value efficiency and competition but would not call citizens customers; split.

positive-liberty.rationale: Friedman and Goldwater define freedom as absence of coercion, and reject the idea that state must supply material means.

media-academia-power.rationale: Conservative rhetoric often charges this, but fiscal conservatism as such has no stated view.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not part of the economic philosophy; Friedman says markets are blind to personal traits, so a mild disagree by inference.

organic-representation.rationale: Inferred: adherents back conventional elected representation and oppose corporatist bodies.

total-state.rationale: Strongly opposed to state direction of the economy and life; Reagan says government is the problem.

national-rebirth.rationale: Reagan's talk of renewal exists, but a radical rebirth from decadence is not a core fiscal claim.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Inferred: costly expansion conflicts with spending restraint and limited government.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority resting on consent and law, as Reagan holds, excludes feudal loyalty.

bound-labor.rationale: Violates free labor markets and property in oneself, as Friedman's voluntary exchange requires.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Inferred: Friedman's empirical economics assumes objective findings, but no direct statement.

single-common-good.rationale: Friedman favors market coordination of diverse interests over a central determination of the good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: No position in the economic philosophy.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: No position in the economic philosophy.

revive-national-language.rationale: No position in the economic philosophy.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Mandated democratic control of firms departs from private ownership and market management.

school-vouchers.rationale: Friedman proposed education vouchers in Capitalism and Freedom, and fiscal conservatives broadly back choice and competition.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Reagan condemned piling deficit upon deficit, the article defines the creed by balanced budgets, and Friedman rejects the Keynesian multiplier.

economic-freedom.rationale: Friedman argues economic freedom is necessary for political freedom, and Goldwater ties property and freedom together.

rule-by-example.rationale: Inferred: limited-government adherents rely on law and constitutional limits, not rulers' example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Inferred from consent-of-the-governed framing; economic philosophy does not address it directly.

force-without-un.rationale: Goldwater opposes deferring US policy to the UN, from which a willingness to act without approval follows.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Not addressed; adherents include both religious conservatives and rationalist libertarians.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred: those wanting to cut welfare costs are likely to limit eligibility; also noted in the movement's welfare-reform politics.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Goldwater and the Contract with America welfare reform stress personal responsibility and reducing dependency.

class-collaboration.rationale: Voluntary exchange benefits both sides in Friedman's view, which implies partnership rather than struggle, but unions are not discussed.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Inferred from conservatism's respect for inherited institutions and property.

dominated-front.rationale: Inferred: nothing in fiscal conservatism supports such a bloc; Goldwater focuses on opposing communism.

workers-nation.rationale: Not addressed; economic philosophy rejects class organization.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: No position in the economic philosophy; adherents split.

ban-interest.rationale: Interest is a normal market price of money, so banning it contradicts free markets.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Friedman argues markets are indifferent to race, and the philosophy rejects state-imposed classification as an expansion of government.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred from deregulation and pro-growth priorities; not stated.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not an economic matter; adherents split.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiratorial claim not part of the doctrine; mild disagree by inference.

national-mission.rationale: Goldwater limits aid and foreign commitments, so spreading a government form is not core; mild disagree.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Market adherents see opportunity as open under voluntary exchange; not a fiscal topic.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Reagan blamed government growth, yet no stated view on corruption of elites.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: State coercion over reproduction contradicts the limited-government creed.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Nothing in the fiscal sources concerns legal accountability for past security-force abuses; adherents split.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Goldwater and Friedman restrict government to law, defense and property, though Friedman adds money and some other functions, so most adherents say yes with reservations.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Opposes state interference in private choices; markets ignore race per Friedman.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Goldwater and Friedman favor equal treatment under law, such as equal tax percentages; an inference for moral worth.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist doctrinal question the movement has no stance on.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Fiscal conservatism takes no stance on how settler states should be characterized; the sources are silent.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not addressed by the economic philosophy.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred from preference for limited state powers.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inferred: such a ban is a market intervention that fiscal conservatives would reject.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Opposed to a growing state and to socialism.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Reagan describes government as having no power except what the people grant it.

trade-surplus.rationale: Friedman and free-trade advocates reject mercantilist export surplus goals.

population-transfer.rationale: Inferred from limited-government principles and equal treatment.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Voluntary exchange and limited coercion are core, but fiscal conservatives accept taxation and state force, so only agree.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Free-market competition as the engine of prosperity is core, though not applied to peoples in the statement's sense.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between order and liberty.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Freedom is conceived as absence of coercion by government; the republican concept is a different one.

separated-powers.rationale: Reagan and Goldwater stress dividing powers between federal government, states and people.

vanguard-party.rationale: Opposed to socialism and to party-led rule.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Goldwater and Friedman reject special priority in law for any group, preferring general rules and market growth to help the poor.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Privatization of public assets and wider ownership are favored, as the article lists privatization among goals.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Inferred from the movement's opposition to union power and general deregulation of labor, but it is not stated directly in sources.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Market advocates ascribe poverty to lack of growth and institutions, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Not addressed by the economic philosophy; adherents split.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Inferred from commitment to elected, consent-based government.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Limited-government adherents are wary of suspending protections, though security hawks differ.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls are opposed because they override market pricing, and Friedman defends floating prices.

party-controls-media.rationale: Government control of information contradicts freedom and limited government.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not addressed; mild disagree by inference.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Internal party discipline is outside the economic philosophy, and the sources say nothing on it.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Goldwater opposes deferring to the UN and Reagan favors national and state self-government.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Not addressed by the economic philosophy.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is unrelated to fiscal doctrine; the sources are silent, so adherents split.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrine opposed by the movement; Goldwater stresses national strength.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Inferred from limited-government principles; social conservatives may differ.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred: limits on power fit the constitutional view.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall is a procedural question the fiscal sources do not address; some adherents back it for taxes, others do not.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Goldwater urged military strength and opposed disarmament, so ending alliances is unlikely, though spending reducers differ.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Banning rental contracts is a gross interference in property and market choice.

people-in-arms.rationale: Friedman wanted a volunteer military, and Goldwater a strong professional force.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The economic philosophy has no view on rural versus urban morality; adherents differ.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National reunification is a foreign-policy matter the fiscal sources do not touch.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not an economic matter; no shared view.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Cultural comparison is outside this economic philosophy, and the sources say nothing; adherents differ.

death-penalty.rationale: Not an economic matter; adherents split.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; adherents prefer local and parental choice but split.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Inferred: Goldwater prefers local control, but fiscal conservatism does not endorse the claim.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship law is not addressed by the fiscal sources, and adherents divide on it.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred: costlier state programs are disfavored.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions from general law are not a fiscal matter, and the sources do not address them.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The fiscal sources do not take up social conformity; adherents range from libertarians to traditionalists.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Reagan condemned borrowing beyond means and hardly would approve default as policy; debt obligations are claims on property, as Burke is quoted.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred: the movement keeps property systems intact.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Rewriting constitutions is outside the fiscal sources, which assume the existing constitutional order.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Friedman wanted the Fed bound by rules and criticized discretion; stable prices as the aim matches his monetary rule, though he doubted independence per se.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial bargaining is a foreign-policy question the fiscal sources do not address.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Goldwater treats property as fundamental to freedom, not conditional on service.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A Marxist dispute the movement does not address.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Costly regulation before certainty conflicts with the deregulation priority.

collective-defense.rationale: Goldwater favors firm opposition to the Soviet bloc and military strength; inference for alliances.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The legal status of annexed territory is outside the economic philosophy, so there is no stated position.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Friedman says economic freedom is tied to political freedom, so trading away freedoms is rejected.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Goldwater would limit foreign aid to friendly anti-communist nations in the national interest.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Goldwater's insistence on superiority and distrust of foreign dependence supports a national deterrent; inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The mode of electing a head of state is not covered by the fiscal sources.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The movement treats the state as a limited servant of the people under Reagan, not as an instrument of class rule, and rejects the Marxist framing.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Goldwater says government may claim an equal percentage of each person's wealth, and Friedman favors a flat tax with few deductions.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Limited government and private property imply keeping churches independent of state control; inferred.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: An economic philosophy with no stated position on the head of state.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Not an economic question; Goldwater and Reagan stressed states' consent and the Union but adherents are split on force.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Goldwater and Reagan favour decentralisation and states' rights, so regional self-government fits; inferred for regions joining a larger state.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Goldwater and Reagan ground government in consent and constitutional limits, not divine descent; inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: No stated position; economic conservatives are split between self-reliance and environment explanations.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Goldwater insists on constitutional limits on government and Reagan on government by consent, so rulers are bound by law.

space-expansion.rationale: Not a fiscal issue; fiscal restraint pulls against spending while enterprise favours it, so neutral inferred.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Goldwater favours checks and balances and federalism but the doctrine does not address mixing few and many; neutral inferred.

leader-cult.rationale: Limited government and suspicion of concentrated power make glorifying leaders alien to the tradition; inferred.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed by an economic philosophy.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Goldwater and Friedman defend capitalism and reject class-conflict theory; Marxist class struggle is opposed.

land-redistribution.rationale: Property rights are fundamental for Goldwater and Friedman, so seizing estates is opposed.

refugee-return.rationale: A fiscal philosophy with no stated position on refugees; inferred neutral.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Inferred: restrained government and Reagan's peace emphasis, but the philosophy is economic and silent on borders.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred from limited government and individual liberty; the philosophy itself is economic.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred from opposition to state intrusion into private life; no stated fiscal position.

common-currency.rationale: Friedman favored floating national currencies and monetary rules; a shared currency is not a fiscal conservative aim.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: No stated position; inferred opposition to supranational political projects from limited-government principles.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Outside the economic philosophy; inferred neutral.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Outside the economic philosophy; inferred neutral.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Fiscal conservatives stress individual choice and markets over Marx's materialist determinism; inferred.

ban-cartels.rationale: Friedman held antitrust should be limited and that state-backed monopoly is the larger danger; inferred mild opposition to breaking up firms.

no-bailouts.rationale: Fiscal conservatives oppose public rescue of failing firms as it spends public money and distorts markets.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Goldwater defends constitutional limits on majorities and government, so courts constraining majorities is acceptable.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from opposition to government mandates and preference for market outcomes.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Fiscal conservatism treats free trade as central; a closed bloc is the opposite.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred: favors free trade and minimal regulation, so binding standards in trade deals are disliked.

moral-incentives.rationale: Friedman holds that self-interest and price signals, not duty, drive productive work.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Inferred from Reagan and Goldwater's support of constitutional order; opposed to revolutionary violence.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inferred from equal treatment before the law and market competition, though the philosophy is silent on titles.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred from Goldwater and Reagan, who ground policy in American heritage and tradition; the economic strand has no curriculum doctrine.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred from Goldwater's limited-government, non-interventionist stance; fiscal conservatism has no colonial doctrine and opposes costly foreign commitments.

patriotic-education.rationale: Inferred from Reagan's inaugural, which appeals to national pride and heritage; the economic strand takes no formal position on schooling.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Friedman favors judging people on their merits in the market and opposes discrimination by law, though fiscal conservatism as such rarely addresses admissions.

public-money-creation.rationale: Friedman accepted central-bank money creation under a fixed rule and fiscal conservatives generally accept bank lending, so a state monopoly on new money is not their position.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Friedman argues competitive capitalism is self-correcting and that the Depression was caused by government monetary failure, not by capitalism itself.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The ideology is silent on post-imperial influence; its limited-government streak argues against costly projection, while Goldwater was assertive abroad.

delink-world-market.rationale: Friedman and the article's free-trade stance treat open exchange as beneficial to all, so delinking is rejected.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Friedman holds voluntary exchange benefits both parties, which rules out a class-exploitation theory of rich-world workers.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Goldwater opposed federal anti-discrimination mandates on private business as an infringement of property and association rights, though many fiscal conservatives dislike discrimination itself.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Goldwater defends the Constitution's limits on government and Reagan stresses constitutional limits, so entrenched rights fit limited government.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from an emphasis on stable legal obligations and limited government, which treats treaties as binding.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred from limited-government constitutionalism, which prefers rulers chosen under law over hereditary rule.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred from a majority-based constitutional order that rejects individual vetoes over collective decisions.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from Goldwater-style constitutionalism, where government is bound by law and may be checked.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The strand is an economic philosophy and takes no stand on parliamentary versus monarchical sovereignty.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred as a mainstream moral view the strand does not oppose.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from a mainstream view that permits farming and research under humane limits.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred from Reagan's reliance on private charity and voluntary giving in place of state programmes.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Inferred from a civic constitutionalism that expects citizens to take part in self-government.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred from a market view that does not hold that mass culture pacifies people.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred from the view that stable order rests on consent and institutions.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Friedman's case for free trade and markets holds that exchange benefits poor countries as well as rich ones.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from individual-rights liberalism, which does not reserve offices by birthplace.

party-own-road.rationale: The strand is an economic philosophy and takes no stand on communist parties' autonomy.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred from the free-market view that trade and investment, not self-reliance alone, drive development.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred from a focus on economics, not territorial claims.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from individual equality under law, which rejects rule by descent.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The strand is an economic philosophy and takes no stand on a constitution's founding values.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred from the mainstream conservative view that both fascism and communism were totalitarian evils.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred from the mainstream historical view that a conservative tradition broadly accepts.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from the conservative respect for tradition and historical continuity.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The strand is an economic philosophy and takes no stand on this.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The strand is an economic philosophy and takes no stand on this.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The strand is an economic philosophy and takes no stand on this.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred from constitutional government in which the military stays under civilian rule.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from opposition to new state spending and entitlements, which paying for care work would require.

filial-duty.rationale: Goldwater wanted welfare-type provision left to families, churches and charities, which implies family responsibility for parents; inferred.

office-by-exam.rationale: Not a fiscal question; fiscal conservatives are split between merit systems and electoral accountability.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from the free-market and free-trade preference for letting capital move and firms be sold freely.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Not a fiscal issue; the economic philosophy is silent and social conservatives and libertarians within it differ.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Goldwater's constitutional republicanism favours representatives who exercise judgment under fixed terms; inferred.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Friedman singles out Social Security as large and unfair, and fiscal conservatives favour private saving over pay-as-you-go state systems.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Private property is core to the capitalist base of fiscal conservatism; outright ownership of land follows.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Legislative control of spending fits the stress on restrained budgets and constitutional limits on government; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Not a fiscal question; adherents split on official-language policy.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the free-market preference for open ownership of property regardless of buyer nationality.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Friedman holds that discrimination is a matter of voluntary choices and opposed employment-practice laws, not outcome-based tests.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Friedman's market-first view treats consumer demand as the expression of free choice; inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Goldwater's anti-communism called for winning the Cold War by active means; arming insurgents is an inference.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from Goldwater's limited-government sovereignty emphasis and the lack of any fiscal case for coercive intervention in allies.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred: fiscal conservatives blame lobbying on the size of government and favour shrinking its favours, but it is not a core fiscal plank.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Not a fiscal question; inferred that adherents are split between sovereignty hawks and open-capital free marketeers.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Tax breaks for parents fit tax cutting, but new payments cut against spending restraint, so adherents are split; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from the strong private-property emphasis in Goldwater and Friedman, which resists limits on who may buy land.

job-guarantee.rationale: Friedman opposes government programs that displace market employment and Reagan's address treats government as the problem, so a state employer of last resort is rejected.

democratic-peace.rationale: A foreign-policy thesis outside the fiscal doctrine; inferred to be neutral.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred from Goldwater's stress on law and order and constitutional order, which treats law as binding.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred from Goldwater's hawkish anti-communist foreign policy, which accepted intervention; not a fiscal issue.

industrial-unions.rationale: Inferred from Friedman's critique of union power and the free-market case for flexible labour markets.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Inferred: the fiscal-conservative mainstream does not hold minority-conspiracy claims and the doctrine says nothing in their favour.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the conservative preference for traditional family institutions, though Friedman-style libertarians might privatise marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from the limited-government principle that public officials remain accountable to citizens, though not a stated fiscal plank.

local-production.rationale: The doctrine as summarised favours free trade and the market over protection, so goods are made where it is efficient.

informal-organisation.rationale: Inferred: nothing in fiscal conservatism favours informal groups, and mainstream adherents work through parties and conventional politics.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred from the Goldwater-Reagan emphasis on national sovereignty and constitutional government.

religious-nation.rationale: Fiscal conservatism is an economic philosophy with no stake in a religious definition of the nation; inferred.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the preference for free exchange between sovereign equals over tribute, and from Reagan and Goldwater on national independence.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Goldwater opposes federal grants and wants programs left to the states, and Reagan stresses that states created the federal government, which favors localities keeping what they raise.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Fiscal conservatism is built on capitalism and private ownership of the means of production, which Friedman and Goldwater defend against collective ownership.

defeat-communism.rationale: Goldwater calls for victory over communism rather than coexistence, though this is a foreign-policy position outside the economic core.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Friedman proposes vouchers so that publicly funded services such as schooling can be supplied by private and independent providers.

religion-illusion.rationale: Not addressed by the economic doctrine; inferred from the traditionalist, religion-friendly conservatism it belongs to.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Fiscal conservatives hold that capitalism and free markets produce prosperity and freedom, as Friedman argues in Capitalism and Freedom.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the view that markets, not economic transformation, widen opportunity, with equality before the law as the aim.

socialized-care.rationale: Goldwater wants welfare and care left to families, churches and charities, and opposes expanding tax-funded public services.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purity is not an economic question and adherents are not drawn to either side; no source addresses it.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on rule of law and honoring contracts, though no source discusses treaties with internal nations.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Common ownership of property and collective communities contradict the private property and individual economic liberty at the core of the ideology.

majority-settlement.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the preference for individual freedom and voluntary choice over state-directed settlement.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Fiscal conservatism is explicitly capitalist and anti-collectivist, so it rejects a third course.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred: an economic philosophy with no stance on land claims.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Inferred: unrelated to fiscal conservatism; mainstream adherents reject it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred: Goldwater and Friedman stress personal liberty and limited government, so criminalising private conduct sits poorly, though many social conservatives in the camp disagree.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Goldwater and Friedman defend political and economic freedom against state power, which rules out suppressing opposition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred: limited-government principles weigh against state religious enforcement; the question is outside the economic core.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred from Friedman's free-trade case, which opposes governing territories for the benefit of the ruling country.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred: the topic is outside this economic philosophy.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred: constitutional limited government implies lawful change, not forcible removal over religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Inferred: Goldwater and Reagan favour decentralisation to states and individuals, not workplace and university direct participation, which is a left-wing program.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred: Friedman treats discrimination as an individual-liberty problem, and the camp rejects class-based analysis.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred: outside the economic core and adherents are split.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred: outside the economic core and adherents are split.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Inferred: the tradition sits clearly on the right and holds it meaningful.

alienated-labor.rationale: Friedman's Capitalism and Freedom defends the market economy as expanding freedom and creativity, rejecting the claim that capitalism alienates.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred: an economic philosophy with no stance on this.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Inferred: Goldwater and Reagan appeal to God-given rights, but the economic strand does not take a position on the source of authority.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred: limited-government and individual-liberty principles weigh against such state rules, though it is a side issue.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred from Friedman's emphasis on freedom of contract and limited regulation of employers.

social-market-economy.rationale: Friedman and Goldwater favour free markets with a minimal safety net left largely to private provision, and reject added state social protection.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Goldwater's Conscience of a Conservative demands a strong national defence and Reagan stressed military strength.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from the argument that growth raises everyone's income and that incentives for wealth creation benefit all.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred: Goldwater and Reagan were hawks committed to the anti-Soviet camp, not neutrality.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Fiscal conservatism is an economic philosophy and does not address succession; its attachment to limited government and merit-based capitalism suggests mild disagreement, as in Goldwater's consent-based view of government.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Fiscal conservatives favour private profit-making credit and markets, as in Friedman's account; user-owned cost-priced banks are a cooperative model they would not back, though they do not forbid it.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Fiscal conservatism wants low spending and balanced budgets, which fits austerity conditions, but Reagan and Goldwater stress national self-government; adherents split between accepting sound-money conditions and rejecting outside control.

property-franchise.rationale: Friedman and Goldwater defend broad liberty and consent of the governed rather than wealth tests, though Goldwater suggested some restraint of voting by those who live off public funds; the mainstream tradition rejects property qualifications.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Not an economic-policy question; fiscal conservatism does not address ecological or feminist theory, and conservatives would not endorse the claim as framed.

reification.rationale: Fiscal conservatives defend capitalism and market prices as the impersonal coordination of free choice, as in Friedman, and reject the Marxist claim that markets conceal domination.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Friedman argues that private ownership of presses and halls protects dissent from state control; fiscal conservatives reject the view that wealth makes the rights meaningless.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Goldwater and Friedman defend the rule of law and constitutional limits on government against discretionary rule, and Reagan stresses a government of laws.

racial-franchise.rationale: Fiscal conservatism in the Goldwater, Friedman and Reagan tradition rests on equal individual liberty and a consent-based republic and contains no racial qualification; Friedman's text opposes discrimination by government.

online-participation.rationale: An unaddressed modern question; fiscal conservatism has no stated position on online participation.

open-government-data.rationale: Fiscal conservatives want transparent budgets and wasteful spending exposed, which hints at support, but open-data publication is not a stated position of the tradition.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Fiscal conservatism in the cited tradition values individual liberty and limited government; Friedman's Capitalism and Freedom opposes state restrictions on private choices, and marriage restriction has no place in it.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Friedman's Capitalism and Freedom argues that free markets reduce discrimination because bigotry is costly to the bigot, so the tradition disapproves of boycotts on religious grounds while not banning them.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Fiscal conservatism is an economic philosophy with no stated view on sortition; adherents split between distrust of new government machinery and Goldwater-style faith in ordinary citizens.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The doctrine is economic and silent on religious law; inferred neutral, as adherents range from traditional believers to secular libertarians.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Friedman and Goldwater treat property and market inequality as compatible with liberty and see the greater danger in concentrated government power.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Fiscal conservatism is an economic strand and is silent on this; adherents split; inferred.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Limited government, as Goldwater and Reagan state it, leaves the state with no role in promoting beliefs.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Even minimal-state fiscal conservatives assign the state the protection of person and property, which requires police and prisons.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The tradition favours limited government and majority-elected legislatures, not guaranteed communal shares; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Goldwater argues that welfare should be returned to private charity and local government, and Friedman prefers private charity to state aid.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits are a common American conservative reform for restraining government growth, though not part of the fiscal doctrine itself; inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: The tradition works through elected representatives under a constitution, and delegable voting is outside it; inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The strand is about taxes and spending and adherents split on funding long-term risk prevention; inferred.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The strand is economic and silent on religious office; inferred.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The strand is economic and silent on household authority; inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: An economic philosophy with no position on local voting rights for non-citizens; nothing in the sources settles it.

rent-control.rationale: Fiscal conservatism rests on free markets and deregulation, and Friedman's market-price reasoning in Capitalism and Freedom opposes legal price ceilings such as rent caps.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from the capitalist commitment to property rights; the sources do not address patents or copyright directly.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from Goldwater's limited-government, individual-liberty outlook, which is wary of state-organised youth training.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not an economic question; Goldwater's strong-defence stance pulls one way and cost-restraint the other.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from Goldwater's emphasis on a strong military and alliances against communism, which favours basing abroad and at home.

recognise-genocide.rationale: An economic philosophy with no stated view on formal recognition of historical genocides.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred from capitalist defence of returns to capital and property; Friedman treats a return on ownership as a legitimate part of the market economy.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Goldwater's belief in a strong defence and individual responsibility, which accepts force in defence.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Not addressed; fiscal conservatism is an economic doctrine with no stated view on national origins.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the generally traditionalist leaning of American conservatism in the scope.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the generally traditionalist leaning of American conservatism in the scope.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Not an economic issue; the sources say nothing on honouring the nation's dead as martyrs.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred from Goldwater's and Friedman's practical, policy-focused framing of politics rather than a cosmic good-versus-evil one.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed; no position in the sources on diaspora and homeland.

culture-before-state.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine concerns the size and funding of the state, not nation-building order.

god-not-male.rationale: Theological question outside an economic philosophy.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Theological question outside an economic philosophy.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Friedman argues in Capitalism and Freedom that competitive markets work against discrimination, so economic roles should not be reserved by group.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Not addressed; Goldwater's preference for states' rights concerns federal power, not ethnic territorial units.

independent-unions.rationale: Not addressed; fiscal conservatives favour free labour markets and are split on unions' independence versus their privileges.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Fiscal conservatism rejects socialism as such, though this statement about the meaning of the term is not directly addressed.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Friedman and the privatization strand favour private or contracted provision over public ownership, so keeping essentials public is not a stated priority.

second-chamber.rationale: Not addressed; fiscal conservatism is an economic philosophy and takes no position on legislative form.

municipal-property.rationale: Capitalism and Friedman's and Goldwater's defence of private property oppose community or state ownership of production.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Not addressed; Goldwater favoured devolution to states and localities, but confederal assemblies are not a fiscal conservative idea.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred: fiscal conservatives leave wages to the market and oppose mandated wage floors, as Friedman argued.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Inferred: Friedman argued that FDA regulation costs lives and favoured deregulation, though the strand is economic and did not centre on it.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Inferred: restrained spending makes dramatically expanded government research funding unlikely, though research is a recognised public good.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not addressed by the tradition; free-market support for private money conflicts with tax-compliance concerns.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not addressed; an economic philosophy with no stated position.

person-over-state.rationale: Goldwater and Friedman held that government exists to protect individual freedom and that the individual is not a means to collective ends.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Goldwater stressed man's spiritual as well as material nature, but fiscal conservatism as an economic strand does not settle it.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Goldwater defended the states' reserved powers, so local self-government resting on powers withdrawable by the national legislature runs against it.

gm-crops.rationale: Inferred: support for free markets and deregulation favours allowing GM crops, though not a stated position.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed; fiscal conservatives favour market land use over planning but take no position on density.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Inferred: the tradition is individualist and holds that people should be treated as individuals, as Friedman argued.

racial-pride.rationale: Not addressed; an economic philosophy with no stated position.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Not addressed; Reagan and Goldwater favoured military strength, but as an economic strand fiscal conservatism takes no position, and adherents split.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Fiscal conservatism is an economic philosophy and takes no position on what defines a nation.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from Goldwater and Friedman, who treat citizens as individuals with equal rights rather than as members of religious blocs.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred: the sources concern economics and limited government, and nothing suggests adherents see partition plots as a major threat.

free-public-college.rationale: Friedman argues that government subsidy of general higher education is hard to justify and favors letting users pay, and fiscal conservatives resist new tax-funded entitlements.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred from Friedman, who treats pollution as a cost imposed on third parties that is better handled by charges than by detailed state controls.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the core argument that public debt is a burden on future citizens, extended here to a duty not to damage what they inherit.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred from the individualism of Goldwater and Friedman, which gives no group weight by gender.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred from Goldwater, who argued for military strength against communism, and from Reagan, who stressed readiness; cuts to spending are favored elsewhere.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from Goldwater, who distrusted agreements with adversaries, though the sources never discuss secrecy in diplomacy.

capital-controls.rationale: Friedman and the laissez-faire tradition favor free exchange across borders and oppose state direction of economic activity.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Goldwater's limited government keeps defense, order and justice as core state functions; inferred.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Fiscal conservatism is an economic doctrine and its Goldwater strand backs a strong military and obedience in war; inferred.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Goldwater and Friedman oppose compulsory union power and favour freedom of contract between worker and employer.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Friedman's negative income tax supports top-ups, yet Goldwater opposes welfare; adherents split.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Balanced budgets and limits on deficits are the defining aim of fiscal conservatism, and Reagan condemned deficits.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Fiscal conservatives favour free trade and the existing market order over redistribution between countries; inferred.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Reagan and Goldwater work through the constitutional order and consent and seek to shrink government, not smash it.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Goldwater and Friedman favour a market economy as the framework, not an open blueprint; inferred.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Fiscal conservatives favour property rights and markets and doubt state-priced accounting of nature; inferred.

sacred-nation.rationale: Fiscal conservatism is an economic philosophy and does not address the sacredness of the nation.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Goldwater opposes federal aid to education and Friedman favours market over state finance, with borrowers bearing their own debts.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Fiscal conservatives see regional inequality as the result of markets and local policy, not exploitation; inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Fiscal conservatism does not address human nature.

public-service-media.rationale: Goldwater and Friedman want state functions cut, which weighs against public funding of media; inferred.

religions-one-truth.rationale: An economic philosophy that does not address theology; neutral.

farm-price-support.rationale: Goldwater's Conscience of a Conservative opposes farm subsidies and price supports, and Friedman likewise favoured ending them.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Goldwater argued for strong military strength and against disarming while a rival holds arms; the economic tradition treats defence as a core state function.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred from the preference for markets and for individual rather than group political economy; the sources do not discuss labour parties.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the protection of persons and property as the core function of limited government; the sources do not discuss FGM.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Equal property rights follow from the property-rights basis of capitalism; inferred.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Liability for proven harm to property fits the property-rights basis of Friedman's and Goldwater's limited government and avoids new agencies; inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Limited government and economic freedom (Goldwater, Friedman) resist restricting liberty for regulatory goals; Reagan's address calls government the problem.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: The economic tradition does not settle sentencing; adherents split between law-and-order and Friedman-style scepticism of state power.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from conservatism's cultural side and Goldwater's emphasis on national cohesion; an economic philosophy does not settle it.

missingStatements.text: Government should adopt a constitutional rule requiring a balanced budget.
missingStatements.rationale: Balanced budgets are the defining aim in the article, and Bloomberg's definition is about not running deficits the next generation cannot afford.

missingStatements.text: Income tax rates should be flat, charging everyone the same percentage rather than rising with income.
missingStatements.rationale: Goldwater says government may claim an equal percentage of each person's wealth, and Friedman favors a flat tax with few deductions.

missingStatements.text: Federal programs outside the powers the constitution gives the national government should be phased out and left to the states.
missingStatements.rationale: Goldwater proposes staged withdrawal from such programs and opposes federal grants, and Reagan stresses that states created the federal government.

missingStatements.text: Central banks should keep money supply growth to a fixed, announced rule rather than act at their discretion.
missingStatements.rationale: Friedman proposes a fixed 3 to 5 percent growth rule for the money supply in Capitalism and Freedom.
missingStatements.declined: Fixed money-supply rules are specific to Friedman monetarism, not a defining fiscal-conservative position; central-bank-independence covers the central-bank axis.

notes: Wikipedia notes that the Republican Party has largely moved away from fiscal conservatism as a cornerstone by the 2020s, and that deficits were larger under Republican presidents on average. Factions (deficit hawks, supply-siders, spending reducers) differ on whether tax rises are acceptable and on defense spending.
